advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Write the run_metadata.json/evidence.json artifact (or make the upload tolerate an empty dir) on the preflight- and PAT-failure early returns so `if-no-files-found: error` doesn't emit a confusing second failure.
evidence: scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:504-507 `runner.preflight()` … `return 1` writes no files
scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:510-516 PAT mint failure `return 1` writes no files; only `out_dir.mkdir` (line 499) has run
only the `finally` block (lines 550-565) writes evidence.json/run_metadata.json, and it is reached only after the agent-run try block, not on the two early returns
'.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml:127: if-no-files-found: error' combined with 'if: ${{ always() }}' (line 122)
advisory.finding: On the two early-return failure paths in main() (LLM preflight failure and PAT-mint failure), the script creates the output directory but returns 1 without writing any artifact files. The workflow's upload step runs `if: always()` with `if-no-files-found: error`, so it will fail with a second, misleading error on an empty directory whenever the run fails before the agent loop.
scenarios: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present but agents extra/config makes preflight fail
Jira DC never becomes reachable for PAT minting despite the readiness gate passing
advisory.suggested_fix: Move the metadata/evidence write into a finally that also covers the early-return paths (e.g. write a minimal run_metadata.json before the preflight/PAT try blocks), or set `if-no-files-found: warn` on the upload step.

advisory.finding: The workflow comment justifying REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=900 states it is 'well above the framework's 250-step (~125-cycle) default (docs/llm-framework.md)', but the documented default is 50 steps (~25 tool calls) per config.py, and the '250-step' figure does not appear in the cited doc.
scenarios: A maintainer reads the comment to size the step budget and trusts an incorrect baseline
advisory.suggested_fix: Update the comment to reference the documented 50-step default (config.py header), or drop the specific number and just say the budget is deliberately raised for the multi-part checklist.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that monkeypatches runner.run to raise LLMError and asserts main() still writes evidence.json and run_metadata.json (run_succeeded=false) and returns exit code 1.
evidence: scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:547-565 — `except LLMError ... finally: (out_dir / "evidence.json").write_text(...) ... "run_succeeded": result is not None`

search_files for `jira_dc_capability_map` shows only tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py references the script, by string, in workflow-YAML assertions — no test imports or invokes main()

ABSENCE: the finally-writes-on-failure branch (result is None) has no test; it is injectable by monkeypatching runner.run to raise LLMError and asserting evidence.json / run_metadata.json exist with run_succeeded=false
advisory.finding: main()'s finally-block artifact-integrity contract is untested: when the agentic run raises LLMError, evidence.json and run_metadata.json (with run_succeeded=false) must still be written, but no test exercises this failure path. The workflow's upload-artifact step uses if-no-files-found: error, so a regression that skips artifact writing on failure would break CI silently, and the ticket's 'every answer traceable to evidence' guarantee depends on evidence.json landing even on a partial/failed run.
scenarios: A future refactor moves artifact-writing out of the finally block or gates it on success; CI's upload step then fails with if-no-files-found:error and no map/evidence is preserved from the failing run
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit test that stubs get_runner/runner.run to raise LLMError, runs main() with a tmp --output-dir and stubbed _mint_admin_pat, and asserts both evidence.json and run_metadata.json exist with run_succeeded=false.

evidence: scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:198-213 — `evidence_id = f"req-{len(_EVIDENCE):04d}"` ... `if len(rendered) > 4000: rendered = rendered[:4000] + " …(truncated; ...)"`

advisory.finding: make_jira_tool's jira_request evidence-capture behavior is untested: the monotonic `req-NNNN` evidence-id assignment and the 4000-char response-body truncation (the ticket's hard 'traceable to evidence' requirement) have no test, despite being deterministic and injectable by stubbing _raw_request.
scenarios: A refactor changes the truncation threshold or drops the full-body capture into _EVIDENCE; the evidence artifact silently loses the full request/response the ticket requires, and no test catches it
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch scripts.jira_dc_capability_map._raw_request to return a large payload; assert the returned string is truncated to ~4000 chars while _EVIDENCE[-1]['response_body'] holds the full value and ids increment.

The count word "three" contradicts the parenthetical list, which contains four relation names.
dropped.finding: The agent instructions claim there are "three UNMAPPED relations" but then enumerate four of them: `duplicates`, `supersedes`, `discovered_from`, `caused_by`.
scenarios: The agent reads the instruction and cannot reconcile whether to report on three or four relations, or a maintainer updates the map and trusts the wrong count.
dropped.suggested_fix: Change "three UNMAPPED relations" to "four UNMAPPED relations" (or remove one relation from the list so the count and enumeration agree).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin actions/checkout, actions/setup-python, and actions/upload-artifact to full commit SHAs (with a version comment) to match the setup-uv pinning convention.
evidence: `- uses: actions/checkout@v7`
`- uses: actions/setup-python@v7`
`- uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9  # v9.0.0`
`uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7`
The SHA pin on setup-uv shows the intended convention is commit-SHA pinning; the `@v7` tags are mutable references a compromised/re-tagged upstream could change.
dropped.finding: New workflow pins astral-sh/setup-uv by full commit SHA but pins actions/checkout, actions/setup-python, and actions/upload-artifact only to the mutable `@v7` major tag, an inconsistent pinning posture that leaves three actions re-taggable at their source.
scenarios: An upstream action's `v7` tag is force-moved to a malicious commit; this workflow silently runs it on the next dispatch.
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-python@v7`, and `actions/upload-artifact@v7` with their resolved commit SHAs plus a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, mirroring the setup-uv pin.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Redact credential-bearing fields (e.g. `rawToken`, `Authorization`, any `token` value) from response/request bodies before appending to _EVIDENCE so the uploaded evidence.json cannot carry a live bearer PAT.
evidence: scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:206 `"response_body": parsed,` — the full raw response body is captured with no redaction
scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:551 `(out_dir / "evidence.json").write_text(json.dumps(_EVIDENCE, indent=2, default=str))` — _EVIDENCE is dumped verbatim to the artifact directory
.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml:121-127 uploads ${{ runner.temp }}/jira-dc-capability-map (which contains evidence.json) as an artifact with `if: always()`
scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:187 system prompt: 'you may freely create/delete scratch projects, issues, issue types, fields, and screens on it as your checklist requires' — broad mutation grant

scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:165 the script itself proves POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens returns a `rawToken` in its response body — the same call made through the agent tool would land that token in _EVIDENCE
gitleaks/opengrep DET criteria scan committed source, not a runtime-generated CI artifact, so this token-into-artifact path is not covered by secret-detection or high-critical-security
dropped.finding: The agent's jira_request tool records every REST response body verbatim into _EVIDENCE (evidence.json), which is uploaded as a build artifact; if the agent calls a credential-returning endpoint such as POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens (which the checklist's 'can the admin PAT create X' experiments and broad create/delete grant make reachable), the live `rawToken` bearer credential is serialized unredacted into the artifact that outlives the ephemeral container and is downloadable by anyone with repo read access.
scenarios: The agent, following checklist step 5 ('can the admin PAT create ... ?') or its own initiative under the broad create grant, mints or lists a PAT via the jira_request tool; the response `rawToken`/token value is written to evidence.json and uploaded.
A reviewer or any account with repo Actions read access downloads the jira-dc-capability-map artifact and obtains a bearer credential.
dropped.suggested_fix: In jira_request, sanitize `parsed` (and `body`) before appending to _EVIDENCE — drop or mask known credential keys such as `rawToken`/`token`/`Authorization` — so no response body containing a live token is ever serialized into the uploaded artifact.

dropped.finding: The admin Personal Access Token minted by _mint_admin_pat is never revoked in-process; unlike tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py which sweeps leftover harness PATs, the script has no DELETE of the token it created.
scenarios: If a future change reuses this mint helper against a non-ephemeral or shared instance, or the teardown step is removed/skipped, the un-revoked admin PAT (valid ~1 day) persists as live credential residue.
